'''Michele Parrinello''' (born 7 September 1945) is an Italian physicist particularly known for his work in [[molecular dynamics]] (the computer simulation of physical movements of [[atoms]] and [[molecules]]). Parrinello and [[Roberto Car]] were awarded the [[Dirac Medal (ICTP)|Dirac Medal]] of the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]] (ICTP) and the [[Sidney Fernbach Award]] in 2009 for their continuing development of the [[Car–Parrinello method]], first proposed while working at [[SISSA]] in their seminal 1985 paper,<ref name= "prl1985" >{{cite journal | last1 = Car | first1 = Richard | last2 = Parrinello | first2 = Michele | year = 1985 | title = Unified approach for molecular dynamics and density-functional theory |  journal = Physical Review Letters | volume = 55 | issue = 22 | pages = 2471–2474| doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.55.2471 | pmid = 10032153 | bibcode = 1985PhRvL..55.2471C | doi-access = free }}</ref> "Unified Approach for Molecular Dynamics and Density-Functional Theory".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.computer.org/portal/web/pressroom/2009/fernbach |title=Car and Parrinello Named 2009 Fernbach Winners |work=[[IEEE Computer Society]] |date=15 October 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111111042948/http://www.computer.org/portal/web/pressroom/2009/fernbach |archive-date=2011-11-11}}</ref> They have continued to receive awards for this breakthrough, most recently the Dreyfus Prize in the Chemical Sciences<ref name = "dreyfus">Linda Wang (29 May 2017). [https://cen.acs.org/articles/95/i22/Dreyfus-Prize-Chemical-Sciences-Michele.html Dreyfus Prize in the Chemical Sciences to Michele Parrinello]. ''[[Chemical & Engineering News]]''. Accessed August 2021.</ref> and the 2021 Benjamin Franklin Medal in Chemistry.<ref name = "franklin">{{cite web |url=https://fi.edu/en/awards/laureates/michele-parrinello |title= The Franklin Institute Awards: Michele Parrinello |website=fi.edu |date= 25 January 2020 |access-date=2024-04-08}}</ref>

Parrinello also co-authored highly cited publications on "polymorphic transitions in single crystals"<ref name= "jap1981" >{{cite journal | last2 = Rahman | first2 = Aneesur | last1 = Parrinello | first1 = Michele | year = 1981 | title = Polymorphic transitions in single crystals: A new molecular dynamics method |  journal = Journal of Applied Physics | volume = 52 | issue = 12 | pages = 7182–7190| doi = 10.1063/1.328693 | bibcode = 1981JAP....52.7182P }}</ref> and "canonical sampling through velocity rescaling."<ref name= "jcp2007" >{{cite journal | last1 = Bussi | first1 = Giovanni | last2 = Donadio | first2 = Davide | last3 = Parrinello | first3 = Michele | year = 2007 | title = Canonical sampling through velocity rescaling |  journal = The Journal of Chemical Physics | volume = 126  | issue = 1 | pages = 014101| doi = 10.1063/1.2408420 | pmid = 17212484 | arxiv = 0803.4060 | bibcode = 2007JChPh.126a4101B | s2cid = 23411901 }}</ref>

==Life and career==
Michele Parrinello was born in [[Messina, Sicily|Messina]] ([[Sicily]]) and received his ''[[Laurea]]'' in physics from the [[University of Bologna]] in 1968. After working at the [[International School for Advanced Studies]] in [[Trieste]], the [[IBM Zurich Research Laboratory|IBM research laboratory]] in [[Zurich]], and the [[Max Planck Institute for Solid State Research]] in [[Stuttgart]], he was appointed Professor of Computational Science at the [[Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Zurich]] in 2001, a position he also holds at the [[Università della Svizzera italiana]] in [[Lugano]].<ref name = profile>Profile: Michele Parrinello. [https://search.usi.ch/en/people/3b1efdf234d1c4d61794f89ef66ac885/parrinello-michele Biography]. ''[[Università della Svizzera italiana]]''. Accessed August 2021.</ref> In 2004 he was elected to Great Britain's [[Royal Society]]. In 2010, he became International Member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="nacad2010">{{Citation | title=Michele Parrinello | newspaper=[[National Academy of Sciences]] | date= 2010 | url= https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/michele-parrinello-zqrt7b/}}</ref> In 2011 he was awarded the [[Marcel Benoist Prize]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www5.rsi.ch/home/networks/retedue/approfondimento/giardinodialbert/2011/12/04/michele-parrinello.html |language=it |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141108004038/http://www5.rsi.ch/home/networks/retedue/approfondimento/giardinodialbert/2011/12/04/michele-parrinello.html |title=The man who speaks with molecules |work=[[Radiotelevisione svizzera di lingua italiana|RSI]] |date=2011-09-20|archive-date=2014-11-08}}</ref> Between 2014 and 2018, he was a member of the Scientific and Technical Committee of the [[Italian Institute of Technology|Italian Institute of Technology (IIT)]]. Since 2018, he has been a Senior Researcher, and since 2020, the Principal Investigator of the Atomistic Simulations research unit at the [[Italian Institute of Technology|Italian Institute of Technology (IIT)]].
In 2020 he received the [[Benjamin Franklin Medal (Franklin Institute)]] in Chemistry.<ref name="franklin"/> As of 2024, he has received over 150,000 scientific citations and has an [[h-index]] of [https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=lnkt9rgAAAAJ&hl=en 163], which is one of the highest among all scientists. In Clarivate's annual list of citation laureates, Car and Parrinello have been selected as candidates for the 2024 chemistry Nobel prize.<ref name="chemistryworld2024">{{Citation | title=Predictions for the 2024 chemistry prize highlight growing importance of AI and computational methods | newspaper=[[chemistryworld.com]] | date= 20 September 2024 | url= https://www.chemistryworld.com/news/predictions-for-the-2024-chemistry-prize-highlight-growing-importance-of-ai-and-computational-methods/4020172.article}}</ref>

As of 2023, at the age of 78, there are still 6 PhD students working in his group.<ref name = "ticinolive">{{cite web |url=https://www.ticinolive.ch/2023/12/13/simulo-comportamento-atomi-molecole-usando-calcolatore-intervista-al-professor-michele-parrinello/ |title="I simulate the behavior of atoms and molecules using the calculator" – Interview with Professor Michele Parrinello |language=it |work=Ticinolive |date=2023-12-13 |access-date=2024-04-08}}</ref>

== Selected notable contributions==
* [[Car–Parrinello molecular dynamics]] (the original paper on this is now the 5th most highly cited paper in [http://www.aps.org/publications/apsnews/200304/prl-5.cfm Physical Review Letters])
* Parrinello–Rahman algorithm
* [[Flying ice cube]]
* [[Metadynamics]]
* [[Machine learning potential]]
